title: King Siva I
biography: Siva I (524–525 CE) governed briefly for one year. His short tenure likely focused on administrative maintenance rather than transformative projects. The rapid succession pattern in this period reflects ongoing elite contestation or demographic volatility among royals.

title: Pharaoh Khufu (Cheops)
biography: Second Pharaoh of the 4th Dynasty of Egypt's Old Kingdom, renowned for commissioning the Great Pyramid of Giza, the oldest and sole surviving Wonder of the Ancient World.

title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
biography: Second Great Unifier who rose from peasant foot soldier to Imperial Regent (Kampaku), enforcing nationwide sword hunts, land surveys, and building Osaka Castle.

title: Pharaoh Tutankhamun (King Tut)
kingdom: New Kingdom of Egypt (The Imperial Age)
biography: Boy king of the Eighteenth Dynasty who restored traditional polytheistic Amun worship in Thebes; his intact royal tomb (KV62) discovered by Howard Carter in 1922 became the world's most famous archaeological discovery.
internationalConnections: Restored Egyptian diplomatic alliances and temple endowments after the Amarna period.

title: King Vira Alakesvara
biography: Vira Alakesvara (Jaffna) (1380–1410) – Vira Alakesvara of Jaffna ruled for 30 years, sharing his name with his Gampola contemporary. He withstood Parakramabahu VI's early military campaigns and preserved northern Tamil independence, maintaining Hindu temples and maritime trade in a fragmented island landscape.

title: King Bhuvanaikabahu IV
biography: Bhuvanaikabahu IV (1341–1351) relocated the capital to Gampola, ruling for ten years. His reign emphasized Buddhist patronage and regional fortification amid persistent South Indian interference. The capital shift illustrates continued strategic adaptation to external threats.
